 Some Social Security beneficiaries will get their 2027 COLA raises early
 Published: Nov. 07, 2026, 12:38 p.m. 
 More than 7 million people in the U.S. receive benefits through SSI. Payments average about $740 a month and go to low-income senior citizens, people with disabilities and the blind. AP 
 Set as Google Preferred Source 
 By Leada Gore | lgore@al.com 
 Social Security recipients are on s chedule for a 3.6% cost-of-living-adjustment in 2027. For most people, the bigger payments will arrive with the first deposit in January but others will get their boost a little earlier.
 Supplemental Security Income payments will be issued on Tuesday, Dec. 1 – the regular schedule – and then again on Thursday, Dec. 31. No payment will be issued on New Year’s Day, Friday, Jan. 1, 2027 because of the federal holiday, meaning recipients will receive their 2027 COLA a day early, on Dec. 31."
 More than 7 million people in the U.S. receive benefits through SSI. Payments average about $740 a month and go to low-income senior citizens, people with disabilities and the blind.
 The 3.6% COLA raises the maximum monthly benefit to: 
 Individual - $1,029 per month, up $35 from 2026 
 Couples - $1,544 per month, up $53 from 2026 
 Essential persons - $516 a month, up $18 from 2026 
 Social Security 
 Traditional Social Security recipients will have to wait until January 2027 to receive their COLA.
 Social Security is paid based on date of birth. People born from the 1st – 10th are paid on the second Wednesday of the month; people born 11th – 20th are paid on the third Wednesday; and people born 21st – 31st are paid on the fourth Wednesday. 
 The COLA adjustment means an additional $75, or $900 a year, for the average retired worker.
 More than 56 million retirees, dependents and disabled workers receive Social Security benefits.
